Building your sense of right and wrong through books, research, and trusted individuals can be a well-informed and nuanced approach. Ultimately, the key to making good decisions lies not in the source of your moral guidance, but in the quality of your thought process and the values you've developed. By being aware of your own biases, actively seeking out diverse perspectives, and continually reflecting on your values and principles, you can cultivate a robust and adaptive moral compass. It's also important to recognize that moral development is a lifelong process, and it's okay to evolve and refine your values and principles over time.
